result.title: Waiting Buys Exactly Two Moments: Endogenous Identification in Prediction-Driven Allocation
result.summary: A planner with a fixed budget of preventive help must decide whom to help and when. Waiting reveals risk but removes intervention opportunities as higher-risk individuals leave first. We characterize this tradeoff under repeated noisy signals and risk-dependent attrition: in the canonical model, a length-$τ$ observation prefix identifies exactly the latent risk moments $m_j=\mathbb E[p^j]$ for $j=0,\ldots,2τ-1$, buying two new moments per additional period. These identify average next-period attrition among survivors but need not identify allocation welfare or attrition among those prioritized for treatment. Our observationally equivalent constructions establish unavoidable timing regret at any sample size for a fixed observation length, while exact certificates determine whether all compatible populations share a unique optimal date. Matched experiments separate the effects of estimation, bootstrap averaging, and regret weighting. Longer observation often resolves timing ambiguity, but the optimal date may already have passed. In our experiments, bootstrap averaging and early stopping improve decisions, while regret weighting adds no improvement in pooled mean squared regret: better statistical fit need not yield better allocation welfare. The code and artifacts are available at https://github.com/KurbanIntelligenceLab/waiting-buys-two-moments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究固定预算下预防性帮助的分配问题，刻画重复噪声信号与风险相关流失下「等待」的权衡：长度 τ 的观测前缀恰好识别前 2τ−1 个潜在风险矩，并构造观测等价情形说明定时遗憾在有限样本下不可避免，实验中 bootstrap 平均与提前停止改善决策而遗憾加权无增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 观测前缀能识别多少潜在信息、以及何时停止观测才算划算，可能与 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的信息—计算权衡构成类比，其「观测长度换潜状态信息」的刻画可供核查是否能迁移到 latent 推理的停止与评价问题。
